Commentary.Commentary: Stuart Broad was an absolute star with the ball. He claimed a 6-fer and played a crucial role in forcing an early collapse. He was ably supported by James Anderson who finished with a 4-wicket haul. Leaving these two alone, the rest of the bowling wasn't consistent enough. So far, all the wickets have been picked by the new ball bowlers in this Test. Let's see whether the picture changes going further or not. Stay tuned as England will be out soon to build on their lead.

A great recovery by New Zealand. If you remember, they lost half their side with only 36 runs on the board and it looked almost certain that England will gain a big lead. But the 142-run stand between BJ Watling and Colin de Grandhomme bailed them out. Both stroked vital fifties but failed to make it big. Although, Watling didn't do much today morning, the likes of Southee, Boult and Wagner, as mentioned earlier, did the damage with the bat and it resulted in England getting only a 29-run lead.

Wow, wasn't that last wicket partnership entertaining? Surely not if you're an England fan. Trent Boult and Neil Wagner raised a 39-run stand and reduced the deficit below the 50-run mark. The day started with the cameo by Tim Southee and then England took the second new ball to pick a few wickets. However, they went completely flat when put under the cosh by the Kiwi tailenders.

OUT! Here goes the last wicket. England finally get rid of the last-wicket-frustrating-partnership. Stuart Broad wraps it up with a 6-fer. This is the 8th time he has achieved this feat in Tests. Persists with a short ball on leg, Boult moves inside the line to pull but gets a top edge instead. It flies towards fine leg where Dawid Malan takes a good catch near the rope. NEW ZEALAND BOWLED OUT FOR 278 and England gain a very small lead which at one stage looked like will be a massive one.
And again! Moves leg side as he knows Broad will bowl short but fails to connect again.
Another hook and a miss from Boult as he can't put the short ball away.

In the air... safe again! Agonizing for England. Length delivery on middle and off, Boult backs away to drive it away but ends up chipping it in the air. Much to his delight and England's dismay the ball evades Broad at short cover. A single taken.
Boult now tries to bring out everything he has in his kitty. Looks to ramp a short ball over the keeper but fails to do so.
This one is down the leg side and the batsman leaves it alone.

More frustration as nothing is spotted on Snicko and Hot Spot! England losing patience and also lose a review! Wood decks in a short ball down leg, Boult makes room and hence the bowler follows. The batsman tries to help it away but seems to have missed it. Bairstow moves to his left and collects it. Starts to appeal but umpire Erasmus stays put. England opt for the DRS. And replays show there is no involvement of the bat.
Is that it for New Zealand? A huge appeal for a strangle down the leg side is not given by the umpire. Bairstow thinks he has heard something and Root takes the DRS.
Bangs again, this time on the leg stump, Neil lifts his one leg up and helps it with a pull towards fine leg for a single to continue to hurt England.
Short delivery down the leg side, Wagner moves inside the line to pull it down to fine leg but fails to do so.
Pitched right up there, driven crisply but straight to cover.

Good change of pace. Boult continues to move around in the crease and had no idea about this one. Stuart bowls a slower delivery on the stumps, Trent makes plenty of movement inside the crease but the bowler sticks to his line. Follows Trent a bit down the leg side, the batsman tries to keep it out but is done in by the lack of pace on it.

These two are putting a good show here. Fuller ball on the stumps, Boult clears his front leg and lofts it over mid on. Seemed destined to go for a boundary but Anderson from that position does well to stop it inside the rope. Two added to the total.
Sprayed it on the pads, worked fine down the leg side for an easy single.
Back to bowling short stuff, Wagner moves away and looks to pull it but it's too high. A good take from Jonny Bairstow behind.
Fuller in length from around the wicket, Wagner looks to dig it out but fails to do it.
A long chat between Root, Anderson and Broad. They need to talk about what's going on...

FOUR! Murdered. This is atrocious, trust me. Length ball, sprayed a bit wider outside off, Boult goes chasing after it and whacks it through cover for a boundary. The trail and partnership both read - 34!
Very full and at the base of the stumps, Boult stays leg side as he jams it out.
On the pads, whipped by Wagner through mid-wicket for a single.
Neil defends it from within the crease.
Appeal for an LBW! Fuller in length and angling in, Wagner misses to get pinged on the pads. The umpire turns the appeal down as it was going down leg.

More runs! Wood from around the wicket bowls it on a length outside off, Trent Boult backs away and smashes it through mid off. Root gives a long chase and does extremely well to pull the ball back in play. Saves a run for his side. The stand moves to 29 now.
Mark Wood is brought back into the attack. So a 5-fer for Anderson seems to have gone out of the window as of now. No third man for Wood so he can't bowl short and wide outside off...
Low full toss on off, pushed towards cover.
Good length on off, Wagner looks to defend it but the ball whizzes past the outside edge.
Shortish in length outside off, NW tries fetching it from outside off but fails to get any wood on it.
Back of a length this time from around the wicket, kept out off the back foot.
Another one on a shorter length on middle and off, Neil looks to unfurl a flat-batted pull but skews it off the top edge down to third man for a double.
FOUR! That's a slap on the face! Broad goes short, goes wide, Wagner stays put and slams it through point for a boundary. This is frustrating England.
Fuller delivery and angling in on middle, Boult looks to flick but misses as the ball lobs off his thigh pad towards the off side. 13 coming from that over.

Chance of a run out! Wagner pushes one towards Broad at mid on and the batsmen are unsure whether to run or not. They eventually decide to go for it. Much to their delight, Stuart Broad fails to gather the ball. A single taken.

SIX! That's a biggie. The deficit now is under 50! Anderson can do nothing about it. He bangs in a short one on leg, Wagner at first was trying to duck but then while crouching he swings his bat. Gets a top edge and it sails over the fine leg fence and into the grass banks.
Stays back to a length delivery and swings wildly across the line but connects only with thin air.

FOUR! Top edged towards third man! Anderson hurls in on a back of a length on middle and off, Wagner swings across the line but gets a top edge which flies over the slip cordon for a boundary. The lead continues to diminish, says Mark Richardson on air.

Just short! On a length around middle, heading in the direction towards off, Wagner is opened up in his defence. It takes the edge and lands short of the gully fielder. What more? It rolls past the man there and a couple is taken.
Drinks break!

Too many open spaces on the off side and Boult finally connects one. A length delivery outside off, it's punched through mid off. Root from mid on hares after it and they take a brace. The deficit reads 61!
Stands back to a length delivery and defends it towards cover.
Broad once again digs in a short ball, Boult stays leg side and with all his might he tries to have a go once more. But fails to make contact.
Now backs away to take on the short ball but it's too high and he fails to connect.
Nearly a hit wicket! Trent Boult walks way across the off stump and tucks it on the bounce towards short leg. He almost drags his back leg on the stumps. Should be careful.
Fuller delivery on the pads, whipped away through mid-wicket for a single.
Good length delivery on middle, Boult looks to chip it down the ground but doesn't get it off the middle of the bat. But still it goes wide of Broad at mid on and he adds a couple more to his tally.
Short on middle, Boult can't get going with his attempted pull shot.
Fuller and curling back in on middle, Boult manages to bring his bat down. Ekes out an inside edge which rolls past short leg and he picks up a brace.
Trent Boult is the last man in.

OUT! Middle stump goes for a walk! What a sight for any pace bowler. Anderson has picked up his fourth now. Can he add a 5-fer too to his name? Pitches it on middle, Southee clears the front leg and looks to swing it across the line. The ball straightens a touch and goes through to take the middle stick apart. Southee walks back but not before playing a handy cameo.
Keeps coming in with the angle and raps Southee on the thigh pad. Anderson appeals but it was heading down leg.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

4th Test fifty for Tim Southee! Certainly in contention for the Man of the Match award is the Kiwi pacer. Picked up a 5-fer and now has scored a pivotal fifty. Works a fuller ball through square leg and picks up a single. Gets to it in just 45 balls which includes 8 boundaries and a biggie. His highest Test score is 77 which came on his debut, coincidentally the team then was also England. Fancies them!
This is good bowling from Broad. Shortish delivery on middle and leg, Wagner fends it past short leg for a single.
Wagner is getting some assistance from the physio. Looks to be fine. He's getting some ice pack on his head. England, he'll remember this blow when he will bowl...

OUCH! Nasty! Broad pounds in a short one on middle, Wagner at the last moment takes his eyes off and cops a blow flush on the badge of his helmet. He's down but is on his feet immediately. Getting a taste of his own medicine? Mike Atherton on air, says he has lost the count of players copping a blow on the head gears in this match so far - Root, Bairstow, Watling and now Wagner. Phew!
Will be happy to see this on a length as he manages to tap it away.
Beaten! Fuller in length and heading towards off, Wagner pokes and misses.
Taps a back of a length ball in front of point and scampers through to the other end. On 49 is Tim.
Almost a replica of Jeet Raval's dismissal. Fuller in length, angling away from off and keeps moving further. Wagner presses forward a bit to fiddle with it. Is beaten all ends up.
Wider on off, easy leave for the southpaw.
Fuller in length and angling away from Wagner who defends it off the front foot.
Strays on the pads, Southee moves to 48 with a flick through backward square leg.
FOUR! Top edge and it's gone over the slip cordon! Southee looks to thwack this short ball but it gets big on him. A top edge is induced which flies behind for a boundary.
Tries to bowl the yorker but ends up slipping a low full toss, Southee pushes it back to the left of Anderson.
Neil Wagner is the new man in.

OUT! 16th fifer in Tests for Stuart Broad! England are wrapping this up quickly now. Both the new ball bowlers aren't wasting much time. Broad goes a bit wide of the crease and delivers it on a back of a length outside off. Ish Sodhi plays it away from his body, expecting some kind of footwork is a little too much from a number 9 batsman and the ball moves away just a bit to take the outside edge. Fifth catch for Bairstow in this innings and he's having a great time behind the stumps. The record for most catches by an English wicketkeeper in an innings is 7 by Bob Taylor. Jonny has a chance here to equal him. New Zealand still 76 in arrears.
Short delivery, angling in towards Sodhi but he is happy to sit under it.
Length delivery, skidding a bit off the deck, Sodhi looks to defend but gets an inside edge which nearly rolls back onto the stumps.
Stays back and with an open face of the bat Sodhi pushes it to point.
Nipping in from around off, Sodhi misses his tuck and wears it high on the thigh pad.
Broad bangs in a short one on middle and leg, Sodhi ducks.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Some serious movement for Anderson. On a back of a length around off, Southee hops back to defend but the ball nips in and beats him on the inside comprehensively.
FOUR! Southee gets a boundary but Anderson wins the battle. An outswinger that keeps jagging away, Southee looks to drive but edges one through the slip cordon and picks up a boundary.
Fuller and down leg, Southee can't put it away.
Sodhi opens his account by staying deep in the crease and clipping one through square leg. A single taken.
Ish Sodhi is the new man to the crease.

OUT! Watling has been castled! A typical Anderson delivery, that. Can't blame Watling here as it was too good for any batsman. BEAUTIFUL! Jimmy pitches it around leg, Watling plays for the initial line but this one nips away, beats the outside edge, brushes the back pad and shatters the off stick behind. England get a breakthrough with the second new ball as they break the 48-run stand and are still ahead by 81 runs. Watling walks back to a standing ovation after a wonderful knock.
Gets forward and across to pinch a single through square leg to keep strike.
Wider this time on off, asking the batter to go after it. He resists and makes another watchful leave.
Good length delivery with a scrambled seam, gets it to skid a touch but no worries for Watling as he defends it comfortably off the back foot.
Brave leave! Tries to bring one in from around off, BJ Watling plants his front foot across and then makes a leave. Not too far away from the off pole.
Hits the length around middle and it angles in towards leg, Watling tries clipping it away but the ball lobs off his thigh pad and dies down in the vacant short leg region.
Fuller in length and right in the zone, BJ prods forward to keep it out.
Stuart Broad into the attack as well. He's one short of a 5-fer.
FOUR! Drilled! A half-volley on off, Southee was waiting back for this. He gets one and he belts one past mid off for a boundary.
Edgyyy. Anderson keeps it full, it moves away a shade, BJ comes forward to defend but the ball shapes away. It rolls off the outer half of the bat through gully for a single.
On a back of a length outside off, Southee without any feet movement looks to defend. Gets it off the higher portion of the bat towards point and they run one.
Now tires the inswinger, Tim walks across to flick but misses again. Wasn't far away from kissing the leg stump.
Fuller this time, some swing away after pitching, Southee wafts at it and gets beaten again.
An outswinger to begin with, curling away from off, Southee gets back and pokes at it really late. Gets beaten.
The second new ball is available now. And England have opted for it straightaway. James Anderson to taste the new cherry first. Three slips waiting in anticipation...
Back of a length delivery outside off, defended back down the pitch.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

FOUR! Edged and through! On a length and holding its line outside off, Watling pokes at it. Gets an edge which lands short of the first slip fielder and then trickles away to the third man fence for a streaky boundary.
Stokes pitches it up on off, BJ Watling once again defends.
Covers the sticks and offers a tight defense.
Fuller in length and angling in on middle and off, defended off the front foot.
Darted in on middle and leg, worked towards mid on for a single.

NOT OUT! As expected. Southee knocks one towards Root at mid on and sets off. The English skipper throws it at the striker's end where Bairstow takes the bails off as Watling drags his bat to get back in. It's taken upstairs and an easy call for the third umpire as BJ was comfortably in. He in fact was near the stump line when the bails were removed and David Lloyd (on air) jokes, he is short of that, should be out. Haha!
A run out appeal is taken upstairs.
Fired in on middle and off, blocked.
Loops it up outside off, Southee drags it off the inner half towards mid on.

FOUR! Boom! Southee spots the flight, wears his dancing shoes on and hits it straight. Jack sticks his right hand out but only manages to get a bit of fingertips on it. The ball still had enough legs to race away to the fence.
Floated up outside off, bunted back to Leach.
Jack Leach to roll his arm over.
Fuller delivery on middle and leg, worked away off the inner half to mid on. A maiden for Stokes.
Is exactly behind the line of the delivery as he stabs it out.
Pitches it up on off, BJ is rock solid in defense.
Stays back and blocks it out towards cover-point.
Fuller again and moving away a touch, Watling leaves it unharmed. A bit of reverse there.
Fullish ball outside off, driven to the cover region.

FOUR! And again! Tim Southee is in the mood to destroy. He quickly moves to 29 off just 26 balls. Playing a handy cameo here. After the fuller delivery on the previous ball, Wood drags his length back, Tim expects it as he stays back and pummels it over mid-wicket for back-to-back boundaries. 9 from the over, 17 in the last two, New Zealand hitting the right notes first up in the morning.

FOUR! Don't even try stopping it, Wood! Fuller in length and on the stumps, Southee backs away and bashes it straight back down the ground. It was hit flat and Wood had no chance to stop it in his followthrough.
Length delivery on off, defended with a straight bat.
Ahead of a length outside off, a nice back foot punch from Southee towards mid off.

Fuller ball outside off, BJ drives it nicely towards wide mid off and sets off for a single. Root gets to the ball and has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. Replays show Watling nearly dashed into Wood while taking the run. No harm done though.
Wood angles in a fuller delivery on middle, Watling moves inside the line and pushes it with soft hands towards mid on.
Back of a length delivery outside off, punched off the back foot towards cover.
Once again delivers it in the channel outside off, Tim has a tame poke inside the line and gets beaten. Maybe, he's expecting Stokes to bowl short.
On a length and just outside off, Southee hangs his bat out in defense but gets beaten.

SIX! Has that gone all the way? Oh yes, this will be fun to watch. Southee has come out with intent. Waits back for a short of a length delivery and pulls it with authority over mid-wicket for a maximum. 200 is up for New Zealand.
Angling in on middle, clipped away through mid-wicket for a couple of runs. First of the day.
Stump to stump line, a length delivery on middle, defended out off the back foot.
Ben Stokes to bowl from the other end. Maybe, Root wants his new ball bowlers to be fresh before he opts for the second new ball.
No, he bowls a fuller ball to start the day, complete contrast from yesterday. Watling pushes it towards cover.

We are all set for the third Day to kickoff. It's bright and sunny at Hagley Oval. Perfect conditions to play cricket. BJ Watling and Tim Southee will resume their innings. Mark Wood will finish off his pending over. What will he bowl? Short? Let's find out...

Pitch report - David Lloyd inspecting the pitch says that it has been an excellent pitch. He adds there was hardly any turn on offer on Day 2. Further, he reckons that the curators have sprinkled water all over it and with the sun beating down on the 22 yards, will make it tacky. Feels batting will only become difficult as the day progresses.

Day 3 is usually termed as the moving day of a Test match. The team that takes the honors today might well be on course to win it. So wherever you are, whatever you're doing, leave it and concentrate on this game because it's worth every penny. We welcome you to our coverage for the third day's play. Hello and good morning, folks!

Twice in a row, we saw a team fighting back from a precarious situation in this Test. What it has done is it has nicely poised this match but given that England are ahead by 115 runs, one would argue they have the upper hand. But mind you, BJ Watling is still out there and with the way he has constructed his innings, doesn't look like he would throw it away that easily. The only question remains though is - will he get the same kind of support that Bairstow got from the tail?
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

After the fall of de Grandhomme, Southee walked in next and would be thanking his stars as he managed to survive. BJ Watling is looking as solid as a rock and is inching closer to a well-deserved ton. They trail by 115 runs and all the eyes will be on him as to how he shepherds the tail. England would be looking to come out and wipe the tail off quickly on the Sunday morning and then bat well to set a target. Remember, daylight saving ends today in New Zealand and as a result Day 3 will start half an hour early. Join us at 1030 Local (2130 GMT previous day) to catch all the action. Cheers!

All this while, Root was left scratching his head. He tried out Stokes (who wasn't deemed fit to bowl), brought himself on, but nothing worked. Then came Stuart Broad towards the end of the day and got them the much-needed breakthrough in the name of Colin de Grandhomme. He was easily the pick of the bowlers as he nipped out 4 wickets while his partner, Anderson was good in parts. Wood tried some serious short stuff but without any success. Debutant Leach bowled long spells but didn't look convincing.

It needed an inspirational batting display to get out of the jail for the hosts. BJ Watling and Colin de Grandhomme formed an alliance and together they joined forces to keep England at bay. They literally frustrated them to an extent and in the process churned out runs. The former was happy to eat time and balls whereas the latter was happy to counter-attack. Both complemented each other well as they steadied the sinking ship through a massive 142-run stand with both scoring their respective fifties.

One word if you would ask me to describe the past two days of this Test - Fightback! Yes, just like England, New Zealand too have surged a comeback which at one stage looked highly unlikely. After bundling out the tourists for 307 this morning, the hosts didn't get an ideal start. Anderson and Broad were running in with the pitch offering enough assistance to them. They applied the pressure by picking up wickets and left the Kiwis reeling at 36/5.

The umpires are having a chat regarding the fading light. They also have a word with the English skipper. Probably, regarding bowling a fast bowler at this stage and adopting the short pitch bowling ploy. Now, they turn their attention towards the batsmen, who are happy to walk off the field. That will be Stumps on Day 2!
Digs in another short ball, angling away towards off, Watling is quick to take evasive action as he ducks under it.
Wood with another short ball, Watling is right on his toes as he fends it away.
Finally connects one. Tucks it over short leg and scampers to the other end.
Once again moves inside the line to lift it over fine leg. Fails to make any connection.

Appeal for a catch at short leg, not given! Moves inside the line to help it down to fine leg. It lobs off something towards short leg where Stoneman dives to take it. They appeal but it's turned down by umpire Erasmus. Replays show it was off the thigh pad.
Taps it in front of cover and calls his partner through for a single.
It's getting a bit too dark for the umpires' liking. They can get together anytime now.
Southee has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Risky single, absolutely no need! Watling taps this length delivery beside the pitch and Southee immediately calls him through. He responds and Bairstow charges towards the ball and fires a wild throw at the other end. He misses as Watling makes it in.
This one shapes back in from a length around middle, Watling fails to counter it. Manages an inside edge on the pads. Hint of reverse?
Once again presses forward to a full ball and keeps it out with a straight bat.
Length delivery in the corridor outside off, a tight defense from Watling.
Physio comes out! Tim Southee is looking in some discomfort after copping a blow on his left armguard in the last over. Getting his elbow examined. Seems nothing serious though...

FOUR! Right between the two fielders. Shortish stuff again, Southee walks across and tries to help it away. Gets it off the top edge and much to his delight it flies right between the fielders at fine leg and deep square leg. Lucky boundary for Tim.
Enough of patience shown, says Tim! Backs away to a short ball and wildly swings at it to only connect with thin air. Immediately Watling walks across and has a word with him.
Shortish delivery, angling in towards middle and leg, Southee looks to move inside the line and leave it alone but the ball keeps following him and hits him on the left armguard.
Much better from Southee! Reads the short ball early and ducks in time.
Tries to be overambitious now! Once again makes room, arches back a touch and attempts to play the upper cut. Misses completely.
FOUR! He's done the job with the ball and now will swing his bat around as well. Backs away to a short ball and pulls it towards deep backward square leg for a boundary.
Coming back in on middle, defended by getting behind the line.
Fuller ball outside off, Watling lunges forward as he keeps it out towards the cover region.
Angling in on middle and leg, worked away towards mid-wicket.

Another edge doesn't carry! Watling seems to be tiring now. Isn't leaning into the delivery, he's playing away from the body. Gets the edge and luckily for him it lands short of Malan again at second slip.
Interestingly all the 16 wickets to fall has been scalped by the new ball bowlers - Southee, Boult, Anderson and Broad. Hunting in pairs?
Back of a length delivery outside off, dabbed with an open face towards gully.
Angling down leg, Southee with one leg up in the air looks to help it away but gets it off the gloves towards fine leg for a single.
Finds the edge but to no avail! Persists with a similar line and length, Watling goes hard at it but gets an edge which falls short of Dawid Malan at second slip. A good maiden over from Wood.
Tempts Watling with a length ball in the channel on off, BJ resists.
Slightly ahead of a length outside off, BJ looks to punch but gets a bottom edge on the off side.
Ducks under a short ball in quick time to let it sail over him to the keeper.
Tries to hit one through the cover but mistimes it towards the same region.
Wood goes fuller on off, Watling shows a nice compact defense.
Short ball, rising off the deck, Southee hops to fend. He does so awkwardly but there is no short leg. The ball dies down safely.
Edgyyy! On a back of a length outside off, Tim hangs his bat out. The ball goes off the outer half of the bat and races through the gap at third slip and gully for a couple of runs.
Presses forward and meets it with a straight bat.
Fuller ball outside off, driven on the up but straight to cover.
Tim Southee is the new man in.

OUT! Stuart Broad does a Southee - breaks the stubborn stand which was worth 142 runs! Some relief for the Englishmen as they have been kept at bay for quite a while. It's a length delivery, seaming away just a wee bit outside off. De Grandhomme tries to force it through the line but gets an outside edge instead. Jonny Bairstow takes his 4th catch of the innings. A wicket against the run of play as cliched as it can get. Anyway, rejoice for Broad as he is one shy of a 5-fer. New Zealand behind by 129 runs.
A harmless length ball outside off, easy leave for Colin de Grandhomme.
Stuart Broad is reintroduced into the attack. Can he break this stand? A long chat between Root and him.
Stands back to a back of a length delivery and punches it towards cover.
There comes the bouncer from Wood, digs it short outside off. BJ arches back to let it be.
Just had a random glance at the scorecard. Isn't it amusing that BJ Watling, a quiet-natured batsman has a six to his name but Colin de Grandhomme, the monster-hitter, has none so far...
Between good and fuller length, on off, BJ presses forward to defend but gets a soft edge which evades through the slip cordon. It helps him take a brace.
Tries to bring one back in but the initial line is well outside off, easy leave for Watling.
A hint of shape in. Angling in on middle, Watling gets it off the inner half towards the man at short mid-wicket.
Goes wide of the crease and pitches it on a fuller length outside off, Watling lets it pass.
Ben Stokes is taken out of the attack. Mark Wood is back.
Finally he plays one, it's on middle and off on a back of a length, punched towards cover.
Four in a row. Outside off, de Grandhomme pays no heed.
Now serves it a bit too wide than the previous delivery, shouldered arms to.
Another one outside off, same result.
In the nervy channel outside off, Colin is too set a batsman to fall for the bait.
Anderson continues to keep it full, serves it with width on offer, Colin goes hard at it. He drives it but cannot get it past mid off.
Stokes pitches it up on middle, BJ brings his bat down in time to bunt it back to the bowler.
Takes a stride ahead, reaches to the pitch of the ball and drives it straight to the cover fielder.
Fuller ball, spearing in on off, Watling has it covered as he makes a good leave.
Bangs one short, angling towards the body of Watling who ducks under it.
Back of a length delivery outside off, tapped towards cover for a single.
Fuller in length and angling in from outside off, De Grandhomme looks to drive it away but the ball straightens a touch to beat the outside edge.
And that's where the ball goes. Straighter in line, Watling plays it off his pads but finds the fielder at mid-wicket.
One extra fielder on the leg side. So far, it was completely vacant with only mid on in place. Now a fielder is placed at mid-wicket.
This one is a little too wide outside off to bother the batsman.
Anderson is probing outside off, hoping for Watling to err. For the moment, BJ is watchful and lets it through.
On a good length and outside off, holding its line, BJ this time shoulders arms.
Reaches out for a fuller length delivery wide outside off and pushes it towards short cover.
Did it carry? Nopes. Anderson bowls it wide outside off, Watling swings his bat at it and gets a bottom edge. It dies just in front of Bairstow.

Drinks break. The current partnership continues to grow and frustrate the tourists. Both batsmen have settled in quite nicely and BJ Watling in particular is showing some great stroke making form. England need wickets. They still have a 132-run lead but it's quickly getting reduced. Can they strike in the final hour? Let's wait and watch.
Lands it on a length and wide outside off, Colin gets forward to cover the line and then shoulders arms.
Pitches it up and outside off, de Grandhomme is forward as he pushes it to mid off.
Good length ball shaping down the leg side, Colin moves away.
There to be driven, outside off, de Grandhomme restrains himself from going after it.
Full and wide outside off, de Grandhomme tries to dig it out but fails.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
In the channel outside off, Watling leaves it untouched.
Straighter in line, Colin works it across the line and Root dives from mid on to make the stop. A single taken.
Just one fielder on the leg side, at mid on. Joe Root has got some innovative field set but it's more to pack the off side.
Fuller and on off, driven past silly mid off to proper mid off.
Way wide outside off, de Grandhomme in no mood to chase it.
Full and outside off, Colin walks across the stumps to align himself behind the delivery and pushes it down to mid on.
Drops it a little short and outside off, Watling hits it from the crease and finds the gap at covers for a single.
Rocks back to a short ball and pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
A bit short and on off, it's punched through covers for one.
Too full in length and outside off, BJ tries to squeeze it out but fails.
Gets forward and drives it through covers for a single.

Safe! A length ball landing around off, shaping back in a bit, Colin de Grandhomme stays back to defend but misses and it goes off his pads to the keeper. Bairstow collects the ball, they appeal but the umpire remains unmoved. Initially, we thought it's for an lbw but later we came to know it was for caught behind. Anyway, England opt for the DRS and the replays fail to find any inside edge. Now, as per the norm, the third umpire checks for the lbw as well but it's heading over the stumps. A review wasted.
Huge shout for a catch! The umpire remains unmoved and England take the DRS.
A touch short in length and around off, de Grandhomme defends it off his back foot.
Ben Stokes is introduced into the attack.
Presses forward to a length ball and defends it on the leg side.
Mishit! Back of a length delivery around off, BJ tries to punch it through covers but it takes the inside edge and rolls to mid-wicket.
Watling has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Bowls it full and straight, it's pushed down to mid on.
On a length and outside off, tapped down to covers.
A silly mid off in place.
Fullish and on off, driven down the ground and the mid off fielder made a sliding stop.
Another watchful defensive shot by Colin to end the over.
De Grandhomme has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Comes from over the wicket and serves a full ball around leg, Colin advances down the track and helps it to mid-wicket.
Bowls this one with a round-arm action and lands it full on off, de Grandhomme drives but finds the cover fielder.
Slower through the air, full and on off, Colin defends it off his front foot.
Flighted and very full on off, de Grandhomme drives it to mid off.
Very full again, on middle, it's hit down to mid on.
Dark clouds are slowly approaching the stadium.
Too full and on middle, Watling keeps it out safely at mid-wicket.
Pitches it full and outside off, Colin drives and beats the cover fielder. It's cut off in the deep and they take a run.
Lets the ball go outside his off stump.
On a full length outside off, driven to covers.
Covers the line of the delivery and pushes it to mid off.
Ben Stokes is loosening up, spots David Lloyd.
Keeps it flighted and full outside off, it's stroked to covers.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

FOUR! Another sweet sweep shot played by BJ! Gets down on one knee to a full ball around off and unfurls his horizontal bat shot through backward square leg. The fielder in the deep can only retrieve it from the rope.
Advances down the track and pushes it back.
Flighted and full outside off, Watling drives it off his front foot but finds the cover fielder. He is timing his shots beautifully at the moment and seems to be in a zone.
Arm ball on middle, skidding in, de Grandhomme gets back and helps it to mid-wicket for a run.
Bowls it in the channel outside off, Watling shoulders arms.
Angling into the batsman, around middle and leg, it's nudged towards square leg for one.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Length delivery outside off, holding its line, Colin gets forward to play at it but is beaten.
On a length and outside off, de Grandhomme plays it from the back foot to the off side.
Gets on the front foot to a full ball and blocks it watchfully.
A nicely timed cover drive by Watling but once again he finds the fielder.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flatter and shorter on off, Watling plays a nicely timed back foot punch but finds covers.
Full and outside off, driven firmly and through covers for a single.
Tossed up ball on off, driven down towards mid off.
Outside off, left alone. 8 from the over.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.

FOUR! Watling has played an absolutely cracking shot! You won't see a better cover drive played by anyone. The way he eased himself towards the line of the delivery, his flow of the bat, the angle at which it came down and found the sweet spot and the placement adds cherry on the cake. Whizzes past short cover and speeds away to the fence. He has overtaken Colin de Grandhomme in scoring. Deficit is under 150 now.
Lands it full and outside off, Watling drives but finds the short cover fielder.

FOUR! Beautiful shot! He is growing in confidence with every shot. Anderson overpitches it around off, BJ takes his front leg forward, nice transfer of his weight into the shot as he drives it straight back past the bowler for a boundary.
Starts with a shortish length ball on off, it's punched off the back foot but finds the cover fielder.
James Anderson returns in the attack, replacing Wood.
Knocks it down towards mid on and Joe Root moves across to his right from mid off to make a tumbling stop. They take a run.
Flighted full ball on off, 81.7 kph, it's driven to mid off.
Around off, Watling goes on the back foot in defense.
Gets on the front foot and drives it towards the cover fielder.
A backward square leg in place.

FOUR! Loopy full ball around off, Watling kneels and seeing that Stokes takes off from first slip in anticipation of a sweep shot. BJ connects and connects well, leaving Ben with no chance of cutting it off. He places it wide, through backward square leg and finds the fence.
Slower through the air, a bit on the shorter side, Watling strokes it off his back foot to covers.
Angling into the batsman, on a length and a hint of inward movement, de Grandhomme flicks it towards short mid-wicket.
Watchful this time. In the region outside off, Colin allows it through.

Colin de Grandhomme survives a rush of blood. Tries to hook a short ball wide outside off, fails to control his shot and gets a top edge. It drops safely behind mid on as Root runs back. Two added to the total.
Short and width on offer, Watling rocks back and punches it square of the wicket on the off side. Three runs taken.
Second bouncer in a row, Watling is not taking it on at the moment.
Bouncer by Wood. Watling ducks.
Gets on the front foot and drives it with the spin to covers.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Strides forward to a full ball and drives it back.
Turns it off his pads to fine leg for one.

SIX! Sweet connection and it has gone all the way! Brings up his 14th Test fifty with an aggressive shot. A knock which started on a quiet note reaches a landmark with a maximum. Flighted ball on middle, BJ kneels and nails his slog sweep over mid-wicket. He attempted a similar shot in the previous over of Leach but that time it had hit Stoneman at short leg. Superb innings by him, he has always played handy knocks for the Kiwis but seldom gets his share of limelight.
Quicker delivery from over the wicket, around middle and Watling keeps it out to mid-wicket.
Good length ball landing outside off, shaping in a bit, de Grandhomme defends it off his back foot.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and defends it on the off side.

In the air... safe! Wood switches to over the wicket and bowls a short delivery on middle. Watling pulls it across the line, right from the middle but fails to keep it down. It doesn't carry to the fine leg fielder though as they switch ends. 100-run stand comes up!
Bangs in a short delivery on off, Watling ducks. Now the batsman will be guessing the length.
Wood alters his length this time. Attempts to slip in a yorker but ends up bowling a full toss on off, Watling walks across a bit and pushes it down to mid on.
Wood continues with his short pitch bowling. A bouncer, going down, Watling lets it be.
Presses forward to a full ball and blocks it safely.

FOUR! Uppish but safe! Leach bowls it full and outside off, nicely flighted, Colin latches onto it and spanks it through the line. Doesn't bother to keep it down as he finds the gap at covers for a boundary.
De Grandhomme has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Shout for a catch! Overambitious. Too full and outside off, de Grandhomme tries to squeeze it out but misses. The keeper collects and appeal, nothing from the umpire. The sound there was of the bat hitting the turf.
Slower through the air again, Colin gets forward and defends it on the off side.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Overdoing it, Mark. Half-tracker again, BJ is anticipating it and leaves it. Should be mixing up his length to put a seed of doubt in the batsmen's mind.
Stays rooted inside the crease and plays down a shortish ball to short leg. Testing stuff!
Bouncer around middle this time, Watling this time decides to let it through.
Nearly plays it in the hands of leg gully. Shortish and around the rib cage, Watling tries to glance but fails to control his shot. It goes aerially but falls wide of the fielder.
Bangs in a short ball around leg, Watling tries to pull but fails to make any connection. Risky attempt with a short leg and a leg gully in place.
Good length ball on middle and leg, nudged behind square leg for a single.
Floated and on middle, helped to the leg side but straight to mid-wicket.

Ouch, that would have hurt! Flighted ball on middle, Watling clears his front leg and tries to sweep. Connects firmly but it hits Stoneman on the left hand at short leg. He has got a lot of padding but not quite there.
Once again Colin drives and this time finds the gap at covers. A single taken.
Presses forward to a full ball and drives it to covers, finds the fielder.
Extra loopy delivery, full and on off, Colin defends it off his front foot.
De Grandhomme has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Some extra bounce this time, Watling is hurried up as he tries to defend. Seems it has hit him on the helmet before rolling past silly point.
Good length ball on middle and leg, Watling defends it down to short leg.
FOUR! Watling is ready to play his shots, unlike at the start of his innings. He spots a short delivery outside off, there is some width on offer and BJ slaps it to the cover fence for a boundary.
Shortish and on middle, defended from the crease to the leg side.
Back of a length ball around leg, Watling tries to work it around the corner but fails to connect. He needs to be careful with a few close-in fielders surrounding him.
As expected, the first delivery is a bouncer, Watling ducks.
Mark Wood to continue from this end. A short leg, silly point and a leg slip in place...
Loopy full on off, it's defended off the front foot.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Slower through the air, full and on middle, 81.8 kph, de Grandhomme flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple.
Colin has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Tossed up ball on off, driven off the front foot to mid off.
Flighted and around off, de Grandhomme gets on the front foot and defends it to the off side. The tactic remains the same with a couple of slips and a short extra cover in place.

Back for the final session. 35 overs left in the day's play. Next 30 minutes crucial for both teams, more for New Zealand as if they lose another wicket, their lower order will get exposed. Let's see how it unfolds. Jack Leach to start proceedings...
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

Mark Wood was really bending his back but just couldn't get the breakthrough. England seemed to be wilting away just like the hosts did yesterday. The current stand is just 13 short of a ton and before it swells to a big one, Root and co. need to come up with a plan to break it. At this moment, New Zealand can enjoy Tea but they would know the work isn't done yet. Can this pair continue to dig in and eat out the deficit? We shall find out once the final session gets underway...

A good fightback from the Kiwis! Yesterday we saw the English keeper-batsman doing it and today it's the Kiwi keeper who has rose to the occasion. Anderson nipped out Williamson very early in the session and the talks regarding New Zealand getting bowled out early looked certain. But... Watling and de Grandhomme didn't let that happen. They negotiated the early spells quite easily. The former was very compact while the latter meant business as he counter-attacked.
Short again but it's down leg, easily ducked under. TEA CALLED ON DAY 2, NZ 184 BEHIND!
Shortish on middle and off, Watling drops his wrists to make a leave.
Short ball, aiming at the body, Watling hangs back and fends it down, making sure the ball doesn't go in the hands of the close-in fielders.
Back of a length delivery on middle, defended off the back foot.
Mark Wood comes running but loses his run up. Goes back quickly...
Switches to around the wicket, another one on a shorter length around leg, Watling gets on top of the bounce and taps it on the bounce to short leg.
Wood comes back into the attack and digs in a short one on middle, Colin plays a controlled pull shot behind square on the leg side. Runs the first one hard, wants another but won't get it.
Mark Wood to bowl the final over before Tea.
An extra slip fielder comes in before this delivery. Leach bowls it full and wide outside off, Colin drives it to sweeper cover for one.
Goes slower through the air and lands it full on off, de Grandhomme is forward in defense.
Shorter and outside off, Colin allows it through. Playing for Tea?
Gets forward to a full ball and blocks it watchfully.
Loopy one, full and angling in on middle, it's dug out back towards the bowler.
Flatter and on off, punched from the back foot to short extra cover.
FOUR! That's a gift really from Root. Watling is happy to feast on it. Gets down to a delivery down leg and swipes it off the meat through fine leg. An expensive over from Root, 9 off it.
Gets back to a flatter ball and defends it down.
Another one on the pads, flicked towards square leg for nothing.
FOUR! Easy peasy for Watling! Root once again fires it down leg, this time the Kiwi keeper doesn't miss out. He gets down and sweeps it towards fine leg to pick up a boundary.
On the pads, whipped down to backward square leg for a single.
Horrible delivery from Root! Fires it down the leg side, the batsman lets it be.
Joe Root to roll his arm over. He came in to bowl a few cheap overs in the first Test and got a wicket as well.
Turning away from a length outside off, patted towards the cover region.
Pushed towards mid off for nothing.

Loopy delivery outside off, Colin de Grandhomme eases it through cover for a single. Third Test fifty for Colin. He has played a good hand again. Came in when his side was in tatters and has played extremely well to resurrect the innings. Job not even half done though.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Dances down the track to a tossed up ball and drives it towards cover but the fielder there cuts it off with a dive to his right.
Floated delivery outside off, a nice front foot push towards Cook at cover.
Sprays it wider outside off, BJ Watling doesn't play at it.
Taps this length ball outside off.
Pitches it up outside off, BJ Watling shoulders his arms.
Back of a length delivery on middle, Watling hops back and fends it towards mid-wicket.
Another one on a shorter length on middle and leg, pulled down to fine leg for a single.
FOUR! Controlled pull shot! Broad from around the wicket, pounds in a short ball on leg, de Grandhomme moves inside the line and helps it along the ground towards fine leg. Played it really fine.
Flighted ball, served outside off, driven through covers for a single and will keep strike.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Very full and fired on middle, whipped towards deep square leg for a couple of runs.
Darted on middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
Loops it up outside off, driven through extra cover for a single.
Flatter delivery around middle, defended well.
Defends this length delivery towards the point fielder.
Stays back and tucks it towards square leg.
Back of a length delivery outside off, tapped with an angled willow towards gully.
Changes the angle again, comes from over the wicket now, hurls it on a back of a length and angles it in, Watling tries to tuck it away but misses to wear it high on the thigh pad.
Digs in a short one again, angling towards off, Colin shapes up for the pull shot but the ball goes off the helmet over the slip cordon. They run a bye.
In public interest - Daylight saving ends today in New Zealand and as a result Day 3 will start half an hour early.
Short delivery from around the wicket, de Grandhomme is quick to duck under it.

FOUR! Poor delivery! Fired full and down the leg side, Watling gets across and paddle sweeps it. Stokes from first slip anticipates it and is quick to get to his left but the ball goes through his legs to the fine leg fence. 100 is raised for the Kiwis, the stand moves to 64.
Drags his length back just a touch, Watling lunges forward to keep it out.
Nice flight outside off, de Grandhomme drives it powerfully through extra cover. There is a man in the deep and hence will get only a single.
Very full on off, drilled towards cover.
Shimmies down the track and drives it back to the bowler.
Good ball! Pitches it up on off, lures batsman forward and then it turns away to beat the outside edge with good amount of bounce.
Sliding down the leg side, Watling moves across and leaves it.
Excellent delivery, straightening from a length around off and squaring up Watling in defense. He edges it behind but it doesn't carry to second slip.
Good length ball on off, Watling stands back and taps it down to point.

FOUR! It was hit aerially and wasn't too far away from the bowler. Broad pitches it up around off, Watling gets forward and drives it uppishly but just wide of the diving bowler. The mid off has no chance of cutting it off. A boundary results. It was the slower one and probably BJ was early into the shot.
Brings his line close to the off stump, on a length, Watling gets behind it with a vertical bat and blocks it safely.
Serves it on a driving length outside off, Watling takes his front leg forward to cover the line and then leaves it.
Drifting in on middle and leg, Colin de Grandhomme presses ahead and stonewalls it. Leach is doing well to hold one end up and testing the patience of the batsmen.
A bit flatter through the air, punched off the back foot towards Cook at covers who once again makes a good stop.
Darts it in on middle, another tight defense.
Takes a long stride forward to kill all the turn and dead-bats it.
Turning away from a fuller length outside off, it's blocked watchfully.
Colin de Grandhomme lunges forward and defends it out.
Stays calm, brings his bat down and offers a compact defense.
On a length on off, straightening a touch, Watling shoulders his arms.
On the stumps, BJ bunts it back from where it came, towards the bowler.
Doesn't feel for the ball served outside his off stump.
Fuller ball outside off, Watling takes a little stride ahead and defends it down solidly.
Hangs back to a short ball and help-pulls it through backward square leg for a single.
Stays leg side and pats it towards mid off.
Run out chance! De Grandhomme drives it towards mid off and wants the single. There is a direct hit scored at the bowler's end by Root and they refer it upstairs. The replays find Colin safe.
Pushed off the front foot towards the bowler who dived and parried it past extra cover. Cook moved back a bit towards mid off to collect the ball. No run taken.

Was there an edge? Nope! What amount of turn for Leach! He lands it outside off, Colin reaches out to drive it but the ball turns away sharply to beat the outside edge. Stokes at first slip puts his left hand out and grabs it. Excellent reflexes.
Good stop, Cook! Tossed up delivery outside off, Colin makes room and drives it hard. Cook at short cover dives to his right and parries it back towards the bowler.
Fuller delivery outside off, driven towards cover where the fielder dives to his right to stop it.

Chance of a run out! De Grandhomme drives it towards mid off and takes Root on. The English skipper has a shy at the bowler's end but he misses. Even if that had hit, Colin would have been home. Good running.
Dragged his length back a touch, clipped through mid-wicket to get a brace to his tally.

That brings up the 50-run stand between the two! These two have batted sensibly and have churned out well. Watling clips this full ball towards widish mid on and gets to the other end. New Zealand getting a move on after that early stutter.
Fuller delivery on the pads, lucky Broad to get away with that one. It's whipped neatly but straight to the man at mid-wicket.
Pitched up delivery outside off, driven back in the direction of the bowler who failed to stop. It rolls towards mid off but they don't run.
Fuller and angling in on middle and leg, flicked towards the man at square leg.
Shot! Dropped short outside off, slapped through cover-point. The outfield isn't that quick and hence they get another three.
Loopy ball outside off, driven towards deepish mid off for a single.
Drifting in from around off, de Grandhomme lunges forward in defense.
Loops it up outside off, defended down gently.
Quicker fuller ball on the stumps, Colin de Grandhomme offers a tight defense.
Floated delivery outside off, driven into the cover region.
Drops it on a length outside off, again, this time the Kiwi keeper makes a leave.

Edged but it lands just short I feel! But what lines from Broad! He continues to serve around the off stump channel, it's on a length, Watling pushes at it and gets an edge. It flies towards Vince at third slip who dives full length to his left but the ball doesn't carry.
Very close to the off pole, BJ Watling covers the line before letting it pass.
Brings it in on middle but it's a bit too straight, it's worked away through mid-wicket for one.
Another one hurled on a similar line and length, de Grandhomme leaves it unharmed.
Length delivery outside off to begin the new spell, a gentle loosener, left alone with ease by Colin.
Stuart Broad is back into the attack.
Drinks are on the field.
Drifting in on middle and leg, Watling presses forward in defense but gets it off the inside edge towards the leg side.
Flighted delivery, landing full outside off, bunted by making a bit of room back to the bowler.
Gives it a bit of a loop on middle, it's pushed back to Leach.
Darts it in on middle and leg, Watling lunges forward and blocks it out.
Very full and fired in on middle, worked away off the inner half towards short mid-wicket.
Floated ball outside off, driven towards sweeper cover for a single.
Angling in a length ball on off, Watling is solid in defense.
A back foot defense by Watling.
Fullish and on off, it's pushed down the ground but straight to mid on.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and taps it down with an angled bat towards the slip cordon.

FOUR! Best shot so far from Watling's willow! A length delivery in the channel outside off, Watling puts it away with some class through point for a boundary. Has worked exceptionally hard for his runs, BJ!
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Another one fired in, helped to fine leg and Wood was present there. He has a good arm and hence only a single resulted.
Darts this one in, around middle and spinning away a bit, Watling gets squared up and edges it past first slip. A couple taken.
Tossed up ball on middle, defended towards mid-wicket.
Watling has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full flighted on off, pushed down towards mid on.
Debutant Jack Leach into the attack again, bowled an over before lunch. Will have the breeze behind him.
Good length delivery outside off, Colin plays inside the line and misses.

FOUR! A genuine outside edge but since it was played with a loose bottom hand it would not have carried. Anyway, there was no fielder there. A length ball around off, de Grandhomme plays it with a straight bat and edges it through the gap between slips and gully for a boundary.
Straighter in line, Colin helps it on the leg side but finds the fielder.
FOUR! Slapped away! Anderson allows width outside off, de Grandhomme spots the scoring opportunity and whacks it through covers for a boundary. The stand moves to 32!
Good length ball around off, de Grandhomme turns it on the leg side but finds the mid-wicket fielder.
Pitches it full and around off, Colin gets forward in defense.
Full and angling into the batsman, 142.6 kph, Watling defends it from the crease to the leg side.
Goes on the back foot and punches it square of the wicket on the off side. A couple taken.

Switches to over the wicket and lands another short ball outside off, Watling has nothing to do with it. The pace is dropping now from Wood. He is still bowling in the high-130s but before he was clocking 140-plus.
Another bouncer, around off, Watling is doing well so far in letting them through.
Digs in a short ball on middle, 139.6 kph, Watling sways away from the line. Testing time for the keeper batsman.

Wood continues from 'round the wicket and bowls it on the shorter side on middle. Watling defends. The short pitch bowling was a ploy adopted for de Grandhomme initially as he was taking the short balls on. Watling will be feeling he is caught in a battle where he has nothing to do.
An inswinger this time but outside off, de Grandhomme leaves it.

Beaten! Anderson bowls this one from wide of the crease, change of angle and that made de Grandhomme play the delivery. However, it nips away to beat the outside edge. Terrific bowling. Using the crease well.
Tries to tempt the batsman into a drive but Colin shoulders arms.
A length ball on off, de Grandhomme is forward in defense.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Fuller in length and around off, de Grandhomme drives it off his front leg to mid off.
Back of a length delivery on middle, Watling nicely gets behind the line and defends it back.
Physio charges in. BJ Watling seems fine but bells will be ringing in his head at the moment. Checks his helmet and gets it changed. Looks good to continue after catching a few breath.

Bang on the helmet! The protective piece behind the helmet flies off and nearly falls on the stumps. A well-directed bouncer, Watling fails to get away from the line of fire and cops a blow. Joe Root is quick to check on him. Wicketkeepers seem to be in danger in this Test. Bairstow took a similar blow yesterday and now Watling. Even Joe Root was hit on the helmet.
Switches to around the wicket. He has a leg gully and short leg in place. We can sense the line and length of attack. Yup, it's short and around off, angling away, Watling fends at it and misses.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to evade it.

Well bowled and well played. Wood digs in a short ball around off, de Grandhomme gets on top and taps it on the off side for a run. Wood seems to have taken a leaf out of Wagner's book. Persisting with the short pitch bowling and generating good pace also. The last ball was 142.6 kph.
Back of a length delivery around off, BJ goes on the back foot and punches it through the vacant gap at covers. Not for the first time we are seeing the batsmen taking three runs.
Drops it a bit on the shorter side around off, it's punched off the back foot but straight to the cover fielder.
Plays it with the angle on offer and works it towards mid-wicket, finds the fielder.
Length ball on off, defended off the back foot.
Sliding into the batsman, a little too straight in line, Colin flicks it through square leg and collects a brace.
Anderson targets the stumps with a good length ball, de Grandhomme blocks it from the back foot.
Lands it on a length and outside off, Colin covers his stumps and allows it through.
A bouncer to end the over, Watling has nothing to do with it.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Watling receives a bouncer now, he ducks immediately.
Short and on middle, de Grandhomme is also not shying away from pulling it. Connects well and the deep square leg fielder quickly moves across to his right to make the stop. A single taken.

Uppish but safe! Another short ball on middle, de Grandhomme pulls it across the line and it travels uppishly towards fine leg. Broad stationed there charges forward to attempt for the catch but it falls just short. In the process his sunglasses falls down and more importantly, the ball sneaks past him and rolls towards the boundary line. Broad recovers quickly to pull it back but while returning the throw, he stomps on his sunglasses. A broken piece now. A couple added to the total.

Wood has gone for a few boundaries by bowling short but he is not backing away from the challenge. Hurls a half-tracker again, around off and Colin shapes up for the pull shot. He fails to connect though.
Another leave outside the off stump to finish this over.
Fuller and angling into the batsman, Watling plays it off the inside half of the bat to short mid-wicket.
Keeps it on a length and outside off, it's left alone with ease by BJ.
Good length delivery on off, defended off the back foot.
Back on strike after some time, BJ. He shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Again, it's on the fuller side and de Grandhomme drives it in the gap at covers for one.
Wood, as expected, delivers it full and around off, Colin is on the front foot as he pushes it to the off side.
Change in plans. Maybe, reverting to the old ploy of pitching it up and getting some movement.

FOUR! Another crashing shot by de Grandhomme. He fetches a short ball from around off and smashes his pull shot to the deep mid-wicket fence. He is a very dangerous batsman and England will be knowing this. An hour or so his typical batting and New Zealand will be back on their feet.
FOUR! Boom! Wood once again is on the shorter side around off, Colin swivels and pulls it in front of square on the leg side. There was a fielder in the deep but he had no chance.
In the channel outside off, left alone by de Grandhomme.
FOUR! There is the attacking shot from the bat of Colin de Grandhomme. Wood digs in a short ball and CdG pulls it with disdain to the deep square leg fence. This will be fun.
Shortish and on off, played down with soft hands to the off side for a run.
On the pads, flicked through square leg for a single.
Colin has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Around off on a length, de Grandhomme defends it well.
Good length ball on middle, defended off the back foot.
Colin de Grandhomme is in next. Big test of his skills here. Will he give the counter-punch?

OUT! The old-fashioned strangle down the leg side and it's a body blow to the Kiwis. Anderson with the big wicket. He is all smiles after getting rid of New Zealand's best batsman. Not a delivery to be proud of but sometimes even good balls go without giving the desired result. Jimmy will take it whole-heartedly. A length ball sliding down the leg side, Kane tries to work it around the corner off his pads but gets a gentle tickle behind to Bairstow. He takes the catch, they appeal and the finger goes up. Stokes also got out in a similar fashion yesterday. These deliveries on the pads are turning out to be wicket-taking ones. With Williamson gone, will NZ be able to avoid the follow-on? Is 58 all out still on the cards?
Good length ball around off, Watling eases himself on the back leg and defends it back.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Hurries up the batsman with extra pace and bounce, it's around middle and Watling goes on his toes in his defense. That wasn't too far away from short leg.
Angling down the leg side, Watling lets it be. There is a leg gully waiting for any error. Good attacking field placement by Root.
Fractionally short and around off, BJ sticks back and plays it down to the off side.
Bouncer to begin with, around off and Watling ducks underneath it. It's always a good option to bang in short rather than bowling a short wide delivery first up as a gentle loosener.
Mark Wood to bowl from the other end.
Fullish and outside off, shaping away, Kane strides forward before making the leave.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Turns it off his pads but finds the fielder on the leg side.

FOUR! First of the innings, finally. Anderson errs a bit in his line and serves it around middle and leg, Williamson picks it off his pads and clips it through backward square leg. The fielder in the deep tries his best but fails to pull it back. Right then, Kane Williamson has now surpassed John Wright to become the fifth leading run-scorer for New Zealand in Tests. Taking giant strides.
Full and angling in on middle and off again, Williamson opens up a bit in his stance and defends it back.
Angles in a length ball around middle and off, Williamson is behind the line as he defends.
We are back for the afternoon session. Kane Williamson and BJ Watling are out in the middle. The skipper will be on strike. James Anderson to begin proceedings. Three slips and a gully in place.
... Day 2, Session 2 ...

The pair of Anderson and Broad made merry on this wicket and doesn't look like they would stop. They have put their side in the pole position and it would need something spectacular on the part of the hosts if they are to come out of this mess. Yes, they have their skipper out there but he needs support from the other end. So far, Watling has seen the tricky passage in his brief stay. 275 is what the deficit reads. The Black Caps have their task cut out. Will they be able to keep the English speedsters quiet? Join us back in a short while for the post-Lunch session to find out...

England well and truly on top. The morning started on a bright note for them as Jonny Bairstow didn't take time to reach his ton. That was all about it with the bat for them as Southee and Boult cleaned them up rather quickly. It was testing time for the Kiwis with the bat as the pitch had enough juice in it and Anderson and Broad came out all guns blazing to exploit it. They were right on the money and speared into the batsmen. Soon New Zealand started feeling the heat and were reduced to 17/4.
Flattish but down the leg side, BJ Watling moves inside the line to let it be. It brushes the pad of Bairstow and runs behind. They don't cross since no shot was offered. LUNCH ON DAY 2!
Darted in on middle and leg, wristed towards mid on.
Flatter one on the stumps, blocked.
A bit too full, drifting in on middle, worked towards mid on.
Tossed up on the stumps, Watling dead-bats it.
Fuller and flatter around middle, nudged towards short leg.
Last over before Lunch coming up. Jack Leach, the debutant is asked to roll his arm over. A slip, a leg gully and a short leg in place.
Watling anticipates it to be another outswinger, he opens the face of the bat and steers it towards gully to retain strike.
A bit too straight this time, clipped through backward square leg for a single.
Very full on off, eased off towards mid off.
Moves away from a length outside off, Williamson shoulders his arms to it.
In the channel outside off, holding its line too, Kane taps it away.
Starts his new spell with an outswinger, Williamson covers the line and lets it be.
James Anderson is back on.
Hops back to a short ball and taps it beside the pitch. Watling wants a run but his skipper sends him back.
Hangs back to a length delivery and defends it down.
Shortish and outside off, climbing off the deck, Williamson taps it in front of point for a single.
Pitched right up there, driven towards mid off.
Shuffles a bit and clips it through mid-wicket for a single.

Loud shout, not given! Nipping back in on middle and leg, Watling looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads. Seemed he has gotten an inside edge. Wood appeals but the umpire shakes his head. Yes, replays confirm there was an edge. Wood denied by a piece of wood!
Hangs back and punches it towards point for a single.
Good length delivery on middle and leg, whipped away through mid-wicket. Once again they run three. Too many threes today for New Zealand.
Outside off, Kane is happy to make a leave.
Back of a length on middle and off, blocked off the back foot.
Covers the line and defends.
Fuller in length and straightening a bit off the pitch, Williamson looks to run one down to third man but gets it off the edge which rolls towards the slip cordon.
Punches it through cover-point and takes the single.
Looks to turn one through the leg side but misses and wears it on the thigh pad.
Watling gets across and taps it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Back of a length delivery on middle, punched off the back foot.
Hits the deck hard, Watling arches back to evade it.
Short of a length delivery outside off, Watling hops back and steers it towards the slip cordon.
Fuller ball outside off, Williamson has it covered before making a leave.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Short of a length delivery outside off, Watling cuts it to deep point and takes three. Still not a single boundary has been scored by New Zealand.
Strong breeze is blowing across the stadium. It has gone a bit dark as well. More of England-esque conditions.
Very full on off, Watling pushes it back to Stuart.
Covers the line and stabs it out watchfully towards cover.
Back of a length delivery on off, tapped in front of cover for a single.
Gets across to a back of a length delivery and tucks it off the hips towards fine leg for a single.
Outside off, no shot offered.
Short of a length delivery outside off, Kane gets on top of the bounce and steers it towards the position where he usually stands while fielding - gully.
This time he stays in the crease and lets it pass.
Length delivery outside off, Williamson prods forward to push it away and is lucky to not nick one behind.
In the avenue of apprehension, Williamson is happy to make a leave.
Watling stays behind the line and defends it down.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Short of a length ball outside off, no heed paid.
Fuller and curling away from off, Watling lifts his bat to make a leave.
BJ Watling is in next. How long will he survive?

OUT! What a judicious use of the review from England! Third wicket for Stuart Broad and he has his tail up. On a length around middle again, this one nips back a shade into the southpaw (thought at first it skidded through) who fails to counter it. Gets rapped near the knee roll of the back pad and a loud appeal follows next. Stuart appeals and keeps appealing but doesn't get the nod from the umpire. He then convinces his skipper to opt for the DRS and they take it. No inside edge on the Hot Spot and Hawk Eye shows it's pitching in line and crashing into the stumps. Boom! England are all over New Zealand here in Christchurch. My colleague says, are they here to return the favor of 58 all out? Well, I don't want to comment on that but what I want to inform is that Stuart Broad now has 405 wickets in Tests and equals the great West Indian pacer Sir Curtly Ambrose in the list. It's a big achievement to be talked in the same breath as Curtly!
England review again. Looks really close again. Broad literally screams his lungs out. David Lloyd says, he doesn't want to comment this time.
Pitched up delivery, bunted back to Broad.
Good length delivery outside off, pushed into the off side off the front foot.
Bangs in a short one on middle, Kane ducks.
4th leave in a row. Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
No movement for Wood. Lands it outside off, it goes straight on, Kane shoulders his arms.
Back of a length again, the line is a touch wider this time, left alone.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Williamson is happy to make a leave.
Mark Wood is the first bowling change.
Wider on off, left alone without much fuss.
Length on middle, angling away, left alone by Henry.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Bumper on middle and off, Nicholls ducks.
Short of a length delivery on middle and off, Nicholls stands tall and drops it down on the pitch.
Henry Nicholls is the new man in. He is fresh on a ton. Can he emulate?

OUT! Ross Taylor departs! Attacking length, screams Atherton on air. He says the length that the new ball bowlers - Broad and Anderson were bowling in the Ashes was either short or good, they were hardly pitching it up. He further adds, they have done it today and see the result. In David Lloyd's words - one of the big shots is out of here. Fuller ball, pitched up on off, Taylor goes for a booming drive but the ball moves away just a bit. Enough for it to take the edge and settle into the hands of Alastair Cook at first slip. New Zealand in deep trouble now. You know what? Stuart Broad has now dismissed Ross Taylor 10 times in Tests. Clearly telling him - You know Ross, I am the boss! The bunny talks can be started now.
Fuller outside off, Taylor leans ahead and drives it through cover for a single.
Lunges forward and blocks it out gently.
Anderson once again keeps it full outside off, Ross pushes it to mid off.
Outside off, Taylor lifts his bat to make a leave.
Pitches it right up there, driven towards mid off.
Fuller ball, angling in on middle and leg, clipped through square leg for a single.
Lunges ahead to a length delivery and punches it back to Broad. Maiden from Stuart!
Angling back in on middle, Ross pushes it towards mid on.
Bangs in a short one on middle, Taylor is quick to sit under it.
In the corridor of uncertainty, Ross Taylor shoulders his arms.
Good length ball on middle and off, punched towards mid on again.
Fuller delivery on off, wristed towards mid on.
On a back of a length on middle and off, Kane Williamson offers a straight bat.
Stays back and stabs it out off the back foot.
Fuller and miles down the leg side, Kane tries clipping it away but fails to do so.

Not out! But it ain't that straightforward as it seemed to the naked eye. As soon as Williamson failed to put bat to an inswinging delivery, there were shouts for an lbw. The umpire showed no interest and everyone including the commentators on air felt that it took the inside edge. But England opted for the DRS. When the first replay rolled in, David Lloyd got excited seeing there was no inside edge. Now, it looked quite close and a good call to take the review. But the replays rolled further, brought the Ball Tracking into picture and all the excitement shown by Lloyd and also Atherton fizzled out. Yup, the impact is just outside off. The onfield decision stays. Michael Atherton on air is amazed on two accounts - 1. There was no inside edge. 2. Williamson has managed to get himself outside the line of the stumps. Technology very seldom fails to surprise you.

Huge, huge shout but umpire Erasmus shakes his head. After a chat England take the review against Williamson. Seemed like there is an inside edge. David Lloyd is quite sure and not impressed that England are opting for the replays. Let's roll...
Fuller in length and nipping back in, Taylor looks to flick but gets it off the inner edge through backward square leg for a single.
Ross Taylor is the new man in. David Lloyd on air quips, the big shots are in for New Zealand.

OUT! Anderson finally draws the edge! He had been doing this since the start of the innings and finally, he gets the reward. Comes running in and pitches it around middle, the angle takes it further away as Raval without any feet movement chases it. It takes the feather for Bairstow to do the rest behind. To be honest, this was always on the cards. New Zealand lose both their openers inside five overs as Raval's nervy stay in the middle comes to an end.
Length this time, in the channel, Kane has a tame push at it only to get beaten.
Fuller outside off, a poke and a miss from Williamson.
Length ball on middle and leg, Kane looks to tuck it away but gets a soft leading edge back down the track.
That should give Raval some confidence! Fuller in length outside off, driven down past mid off. Won't get a boundary but will get three.

How did that miss the stumps? How? The look on Broad's face, he just can't believe it. Nor can I. On a length around middle and off, Raval plants his front foot forward and doesn't offer any shot. The ball nips back in and goes over the off pole.
Good shot! An overpitched delivery outside off, Williamson leans across and drives it through the gap at covers. Picks up another three.

Beaten again! Jeet Raval doesn't have any clue about this. Anderson lands it on a length around middle, Raval is very tentative about what to do. He commits himself to play at it first but then withdraws his bat. Almost kisses the outside edge of his bat.
Full and shaping away, nothing doing from Jeet.
Keeps it fuller on middle and off, Jeet Raval tries to defend it with soft hands. The edge is taken but it goes along the ground towards the fourth slip fielder.

Not the line to bowl, Jimmy. Drifts it on the pads, easy for Kane as he works it neatly past Broad at mid on. The English pacer gives it a chase and does well to stop it inside the rope. Comfortable three runs taken.
Hits the back of a length mark, it's around middle and off, Jeet punches it past point and pinches one.
Anderson sprays it wider outside off, Raval is happy to let it pass. There are five slips in place, not a regular sight this.
Fuller and on the stumps, worked past short leg for a single. A successful first over from Stuart Broad.
Good length delivery, angling in on middle and leg, clipped through the vacant mid-wicket region. It helps Williamson pick up three runs.
Keeps it nice and full outside off, Kane Williamson lunges forward and taps it away towards the off side.
Kane Williamson is in next, replacing Latham. Four slips and a short leg for the Kiwi skipper.

OUT! Gone! Stuart Broad draws first blood! Tom Latham doesn't even open his account, early dent for the hosts. Fuller in length, enticing the batsman to have a go. He does sans any feet movement and there is enough movement for Broad to catch the outside edge of Latham's bat. Bairstow behind the stumps takes an easy catch. You just cannot keep him out of the game, chirps Mark Richardson on air. Another flop show from Latham, he has struggled to get going. Stroked a century back in January 2017 and since then has managed only a couple of 50-plus scores. A lull in his Test career.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for the batsman.
Fuller in length on middle and leg, Tom Latham looks to jam it out but gets an inside edge towards short leg.
Stuart Broad to have a go from the other end.
Make that three in a row! Superb from Jimmy. The outswinger, Raval once again has a poke at it but gets beaten all ends up. A maiden to kickoff the second innings.
Beautiful bowling! Anderson is a treat to watch when he makes the ball move around. Once again lands it around middle and then it jags away. Beats the outside edge.
Pitches it around middle and leg, Raval plays for the initial line but the ball moves away and beats him comprehensively.
Fuller on leg, kept out towards mid-wicket.
Back of a length delivery, just outside off, Raval gets squared up a touch as he defends it towards point off the back foot.
Swing straightaway for Anderson! Lands it on a length around off, it swings away after pitching, Raval makes a watchful leave.
